title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 22: What the Stall Is For

planning.voiceReason: Small practical mistakes and gentle self-directed humour expose Jon’s grand ideas about helping; no change to his age or identity.
planning.earlyCare: Jon wants workers to eat and the centre to have supplies.
planning.desire: Raise a transparent supplies budget without making visitors feel poor.
planning.obstacle: Grand banquet ambitions, prices and exaggerated honey advertising.
planning.dramaticChange: Jon accepts that good soup matters more than looking grand; the cook corrects her claims.
sceneActivities: Jon prepares a comically solemn speech beside a small soup bowl; serving and accounting happen in the courtyard.

actingSignature.Jonathan: Self-directed humour and practical questions; open palms become quiet attention when corrected.
actingSignature.Min: Worries about appearances but now asks whose needs a decision serves; gentle teasing.
actingSignature.Tavi: Proud practical cook; starts defending her stall, then corrects the sign without excuses.
actingSignature.Orr: Smooth confident vendor; evasive when asked for checkable evidence.
actingSignature.Ryn: Specific technical limits, insists on matching materials to inspected requirements.
actingSignature.Sela: Patient questions that require plain explanations rather than impressive language.

planning.listenerTurn: Tavi tells Jon a meal need not be a performance; listener Jonathan then lowers his speech notes.
planning.payoff: The stall raises a documented supplies budget without changing the drinking-water inventory offscreen; preparations can continue.
planning.freshQuestion: A confident vendor promises an instant repair and tries to sell a decorative upgrade as essential. Jon notices a clever use of true details to hide a false promise. A learner's question from a philosophy reading forces him to explain his reasoning plainly. The crew checks evidence, refuses the offer and uses the agreed budget for necessary materials.

teaser.moment: Jon looks from his grand speech notes to one small bowl, amused at himself.

continuation.end: Tavi and Min complete the courtyard food stall. Tavi withdraws unsupported honey claims and explains the correction. Costs, her pay, income and remaining supplies funds are recorded; the funds are restricted to agreed centre supplies. Tavi brought the soup ingredients, cooking water and documented purchased honey; no station water or garden honey was used. Seedlings remain promised but undelivered. The centre remains closed pending repairs. Jon replaces an elaborate banquet speech with listening and a simple shared meal.
